newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end slightly down on sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end slightly down on sluggish trade.

text.p: Several bouts of buying in the late afternoon on Friday failed to lift Thai stocks which ended slightly lower in thin trade, brokers said.
Steady selling earlier in the day, as regional markets dipped, outweighed late buying, they added.

"The market sentiment wasn't good today as investors were quite worried that the U.S. Federal Reserve which is to meet next week would hike its rates. Declines in several regional markets today also brought negative sentiment to the SET," said Thaneit Khantigaroon of Ekachart Finance and Securities.
The SET index ended 0.99 point lower at 702.10 on 2.3 billion baht turnover.
Brokers said some investors believed that the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike rates by 25 basis points when it meets on Tuesday.
"The index moved sideways throughout the session today because of investor concern that if the U.S. hikes rates, it would affect rates in Thailand," Thaneit said.
Brokers said foreign investors were not active. Total net buying by foreigners on Thursday amounted to 531 million baht.
TelecomAsia topped the active list, falling 0.50 baht to 43.75. Krung Thai Bank gained 0.50 to 36.25.
